summary: Measured association between short preceding RR and stroke/filling volume; not universal RR-to-volume calibration.
Beatwise performance depends on cycle length, preload, afterload and contractility.
Primary haemodynamic study reports absent aortic valve opening with very short cycles or short cycles after long cycles; it does not establish our thresholds or a mandatory RV response.
Primary matched-average-rate study supports an independent haemodynamic effect of irregular RR; not numeric calibration.

authored_choices.durationScaling: none; preserve channel baseline ejection and morphology durations

invariants: Coarse and fine AF share events and gain
Gain uses original electrical/mechanical ordinal and immediately preceding electrical RR, never accumulated ejection history
Pressure input and contour use linear beat strength once; optical pulse uses the same gain
No random state, epoch scan or added beats; zero gain only in explicitly opted-in systemic example
Opt-in flags default false and reject unrelated rhythms or simultaneous premature weighting
limitations: Continuous RR-dependent teaching filling approximation, not a calibrated AF stroke-volume model; no coordinated normal atrial contraction
One authored systemic pulse-deficit example; no pulse detection, quantitative pulse-deficit reporting or general filling/valve model
No AF aberrancy, CVP filling, independent right-heart or optical SpO2 calibration
Same ABP/PA gain is a simplified coupled teaching choice, not validated biventricular haemodynamics
Preserving PA/CVP when selecting a systemic deficit does not assert that real RV/venous haemodynamics are invariant.
No contractile restitution or preload/afterload feedback; preceding RR alone does not represent all AF haemodynamics
